# CV-0 spike 2 — the chat store and its device copy

> Branch `t/maciej/cv-0-s2-store` · harness at `d54379a7` · status: built, not landed
> Migration: none. The server half is a draft, [`drafts/store.sql`](drafts/store.sql), proven in the scratch schema `spike_s2` on the local stack and dropped after every run (checked: no `spike_s2` left). Nothing in `src/`, `supabase/migrations` or `public`.

## Delivered against the row

- **The harness, `scripts/spikes/chat/s2/`**, one runner for every bar: `bun scripts/spikes/chat/s2/run.ts [sql] [browser] [access] [--keep]` (all three when none is named; ~6 min), then `bun scripts/spikes/chat/s2/summary.ts` for the tables. Results land in `$TMPDIR/moduo-spike-s2/`. Local stack only (the connection refuses anything but `127.0.0.1:54322`).
  - `sql-proof.ts`: bar 3 (delta = full read, keyset pages over a tie).
  - `browser-bench.ts`: bars 1, 2, 4 and the measurements behind 6, in Playwright's Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing build, new headless), each cold open in a fresh browser process on a persistent profile; the page is served at `http://spike.local/` through Playwright's router so IndexedDB has a real origin.
  - `access-proof.ts`: bar 5, SQL → the store in Chromium → IndexedDB.
  - `page/device-copy.ts` (the device copy, raw IndexedDB), `page/chat-store.ts` (memory windows, apply, reconcile), `page/fixture.ts` (v2 row shape, a body mix heavier than real chat), `page/main.ts` + `page/worker.ts` (the bench page).
- **The draft, `docs/build/chat-v2/drafts/store.sql`**: the v2 columns the store reads, the `zz_stamp_updated_at` trigger, the stream and delta indexes, `chat_can_read` with v2's two conditions, `chat_sync_ids`, keyset page and delta functions; "CV-1:" notes say where the real migration differs.

Machine: Apple Silicon Mac, with two other builders running browsers at the same time (some relaunches timed out and were retried; timings are from completed runs only).

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **Raw IndexedDB, no library** (what `src/lib/sync/` uses): agent · the device copy is ~250 lines (`page/device-copy.ts`) and clears every bar with room · rejected: Dexie (the blueprint's fallback; nothing needed beyond compound-key ranges and range deletes) and **Tasks' `SyncCache` record per workspace**: reading 10,000 messages back as one record took 50.8 / 60.6 ms (vs 1.4 for the range read), and every save rewrites the whole record, 17.9 ms of main thread at 10,000 rows (over bar 2, and it grows with the workspace).
- **Key `[workspaceId, channelId, at, id]`** (`at` = `created_at` in microseconds) with a unique `byId` index: agent · a conversation is one key range: the newest 50 in 1.4 ms whatever its size (500 rows: 1.5; 10,000: 1.4); dropping a conversation or evicting its oldest rows is one range delete (a 500-row write plus eviction: 53 ms wall) · rejected: the id as key with an ordering index (read 2.9 ms; eviction walks and deletes row by row: 354 ms wall).
- **Newest page = a key cursor that jumps back 49, then one `getAll`** (2 requests): agent · 1.4 vs 2.0 ms · rejected: walking a cursor 50 steps.
- **Cap: 500 per conversation on the device, least recently opened conversation evicted past ~20,000 per workspace; ≤ 1,500 per open window in memory**: agent · read cost doesn't depend on size, so the cap is about disk: ~1.3 KB per message on disk (LevelDB, compressed) → ~26 MB per full workspace; eviction rides the write's transaction at no main-thread cost (3.0 vs 3.0 ms); 1,500 in memory is +1.8 MB · rejected: no cap (one 10,000-message channel ≈ 13 MB), 1,500 on the device (history past 500 comes from the server by keyset).
- **Its own database (`moduo-chat`), not Tasks' `moduo-sync`; no worker**: agent · in Chromium all databases of an origin share one backing store: with another database already open, opening the chat one costs 0.2 / 0.4 ms (the first open in a fresh process is the 36 ms in bar 1, which Tasks' store pays at boot); its own database means its own versions and upgrades (Tasks' opener creates only its store and re-opens a version up when it's missing, which would close the other's connection) and its own wipe. Tasks has no worker. A worker cut the main thread's share of a 500-row write from 3.0 to 0.5 ms, but the rows must reach the main thread to render anyway · rejected: a worker now; **instead persist in transactions of ≤ 200 rows** (at the measured 4× rate, ~0.027 ms a row, that's ≤ ~5.5 ms on a slow machine; derived, not measured); revisit if CV-3's perf fixture shows long tasks.
- **`chat_sync_ids` answers three kinds: `conversation`, `member`, `moved_away`, plus `checked_at`**: agent · `moved_away` reads the `moved_out` lines (written in the source, in conversations you can still read, since your last check) and returns the ids now somewhere you can't read or gone; a second move overwrites `moved_from_channel_id`, the line doesn't · rejected: comparing each held conversation's message ids (up to 500 ids × every conversation on the device, every 10 minutes; estimated, not measured), and a `moved_from_channel_id` lookup.
- **Keyset reads as row comparisons in SQL** (an RPC for history pages): agent · `(created_at, id) < ($t, $id)` is an index condition (0.04 ms at mid-history); PostgREST's `or=` spelling uses the index for order only and filters (4,884 rows filtered, 1.7 ms at depth 5,000, growing with depth). Deltas can stay PostgREST if they keep the extra `updated_at >= since` bound (then both forms are an index range, 0.06–0.14 ms) · rejected: `or=` for history.

## Gotchas (area: supabase · store · tooling)

- **(supabase)** A delta test whose rows were all written inside the 5-minute lookback proves nothing: every "delta" is a full read (the first run here re-read all 11,120). Seed with `updated_at = created_at` with the stamp trigger disabled.
- **(supabase)** Stamps and keyset positions must travel as text: a JS `Date` drops the microseconds and a keyset page repeats or skips rows at the boundary (PostgREST returns text; `Bun.sql` returns `Date`, so the harness selects `to_char(…US)`).
- **(store)** With a unique `byId` index, a moved row's `put` (its key changed with `channel_id`) aborts the **whole** transaction unless the old key is deleted first. Only a move changes `channel_id`, so only rows with `moved_at` need the lookup (`device-copy.ts` `put`).
- **(store)** A failed IndexedDB transaction rejects with a `DOMException`, which Playwright reports as `null`: wrap it in an `Error` with its name.
- **(tooling)** `Bun.sql` double-encodes a string parameter cast `$n::jsonb` (a JSON string is stored, not an object): cast `$n::text::jsonb`.
- **(tooling)** Persistent-context relaunches on a Mac shared with other builders sometimes time out or lose the browser mid-run; the bench gives each browser session a deadline and retries it in a new process.

## For later blocks

- **CV-1 (columns, trigger, `chat_sync_ids`):**
  - `updated_at` on `chat_messages` and `chat_members`, and the `zz_stamp_updated_at` trigger (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, `clock_timestamp()`) on all three tables (`chat_channels.updated_at` exists but nothing stamps it). Add the column without a volatile default (that rewrites the table), backfill `greatest(created_at, edited_at, deleted_at, pinned_at, last_reply_at)` with the trigger off, then set the default and `not null`.
  - Indexes: `(channel_id, created_at, id)` replacing v1's partial `chat_messages_channel_idx` (v2 replies live in the stream), and `(workspace_id, updated_at, id)` for the delta. `analyze` after.
  - `chat_sync_ids(p_workspace_id, p_since)` as drafted, SECURITY DEFINER on `auth.uid()` through the real `chat_can_read_channel` (plus `deleted_at is null`, `left_at is null`); time it with the live permission functions on a workspace with a few hundred channels.
  - The move op writes the moved rows **before** its two event lines (the delta then sees a row re-filed before the line that names it); `chat_op_delete_channel` touches every member's row; the event's `ids` array is what `chat_sync_ids` reads.
  - A keyset history RPC (`chat_messages_page` in the draft) rather than PostgREST's `or=`.
- **CV-3 (the store):** the shape in `page/device-copy.ts` + `page/chat-store.ts`: database `moduo-chat`; `messages` keyed `[workspaceId, channelId, at, id]` with a unique `byId`; one `meta` record per `person:workspace` (`conversations{openedAt, newestAt}`, the delta cursor, `accessSince`, the outbox, drafts). Apply rule: newer server stamp lands, an equal one is your echo; a move re-files; a `moved_out` line drops its ids. Reconcile also keeps rows that arrived after the check started (Tasks' `seenAt` guard; the sketch only handles re-filed rows). **The check only sees conversations the store knows it holds** (memory windows ∪ `meta.conversations`): the workspace-wide delta brings rows for conversations never opened, so either register every conversation the store writes rows for in `meta.conversations` on its first persist, or persist no rows for conversations not held. Otherwise a later "made private" leaves those rows on the device for good (bar 5 passed because the harness registered every conversation it wrote). Persist throttled, ≤ 200 rows a transaction, eviction in the same transaction. Wipe `moduo-chat` wherever `wipeSyncCopies` / `attachSyncUser` wipe Tasks' copy (sign-out, another person signing in, account deletion). The 5-minute lookback re-reads the last 5 minutes on every delta (984 rows in the spike's busy minute): run deltas on rejoin, focus and online, never per message.
- **CV-4 / spike 1:** the first 50 rows are in memory ~2 ms after the database is open; the paint, not the store, is the budget.
